note: Does the right Domain Pack get selected when several are loaded? Three bands. `clear` uses one domain's vocabulary and nobody else's. `shared_vocabulary` is the trap: another loaded domain uses the same words (temperature belongs to thermal and battery both), so only the discriminating terms decide. `out_of_scope` are real engineering questions no loaded domain covers, where naming any domain is wrong. Measured against the example corpora in domains/*/examples, which are invented -- this benchmark tests discrimination between domains, not accuracy within one.

removed_band.why: Two cases were labelled `ambiguous` on the author's intuition that their wording spanned two fields, and neither survived checking against the corpora. RT-031 ('cell temperature rise ... pack thermal runaway') reads as thermal-and-battery, but the thermal corpus contains no occurrence of cell, pack or runaway; only `temperature` is shared, which makes it a shared_vocabulary case. RT-032 ('fixture wear ... dimensional capability') names four terms that appear in the manufacturing corpus and none of them anywhere else. The six example corpora are subject-disjoint -- no two describe the same artefact or event -- so no genuinely ambiguous question exists over them, and inventing one would have meant writing a document to create the overlap. The router's requires_human path is covered instead by tests/test_domain_router.py, which builds two packs over deliberately overlapping corpora. Recorded rather than deleted: the benchmark was wrong and the measurement was right, and a label corrected silently is indistinguishable from a label tuned to make a score look better.
